name: Vector-to-Raster Conversion via Sparse Boundary Grids
definition: A two-stage algorithm to convert a set of non-overlapping, closed polyhedra (or polygons) into a fully occupied 3D (or 2D) grid of voxels (or pixels). The first stage creates a 'sparse boundary grid' from vector boundaries; the second stage fills the interior to create a 'full pixel/voxel grid' where every voxel has a value.
summary: This method converts closed polyhedra into voxel grids by decoupling boundary extraction from interior filling, using bitwise XOR operations to handle any watertight primitive with uniform complexity.
